mission.title: Cause and Effect
mission.description: Seize the control terminal of a construct portal and follow the trail of the Effectuator.

npc.say: Next room, operative. This one is so five-minutes-ago.

phase.briefing: Well, if it isn't {player}. We've used that data you got on the dire lupines and their "Effectuator" leader to zero in on a computer system in the City that controls one of the Merovingian's constructs. I don't think I need to remind you how important it is that we disrupt the Merovingian's construct network, do I? Right. So, you're going to secure this computer system, then use it to track down and infiltrate the construct portal. Get moving.

enter.say: I'm picking up strange, shifting signals in there--probably more of those dire lupines.
The computer in that room is the one Zion identified as the construct portal control terminal. It looks like you'll need a key disk to access it. Time to ransack the place.

objective.text: Search the place for a key

done.say: Hey, a key. That might prove useful.
The safe in that room is locked.
That disk could come in handy.
That's a key disk. We can use it to access their computer.

objective.text: Search the computer for the construct portal's location

done.say: Great, you've gained access to the system. Now search it for portal control routines.
Good; I can track that network address to find the portal. You're all done there.

phase.briefing: Now that we've captured the control terminal for the portal, you should have no problem with the portal shutting down before you get to it. But there's no point in taking chances, is there? So hurry up and get over there.

enter.say: That's the place. The readings I'm getting are consistent with what we've seen from construct portals before. Looks like we'll finally get to see one before it shuts down.
The far door is the construct portal. It's still active. You'd better take out those guards first, though.

done.say: Great, now see if the portal-- What? Someone's just appeared in there!

talk.say:
Why, hello there, operative. Nice day, isn't it? Yes, I'm that fellow you've been wondering about: the Effectuator. Oh, don't bother trying to threaten me; you can't hurt me. Nobody can. A happy arrangement, don't you think?
But we're getting behind schedule. Why don't you proceed on to the next room? Oh, I've shut the portal down, by the way. Just go on through the door.

done.say: This is too weird. I guess you'd better play along until we find out what he's up to.

objective.text: Follow the Effectuator to the next room

talk.say: Huh? The signal from the program in that room matches the one from the previous room exactly. Is he cloning himself?

Yes, it's still me. I have no corporeal existence in this simulation, you see? So I can just flit around wherever I need to. I feel a little less real than even the average Exile--we're all a tad insecure about that, actually--but there are compensations.
Speaking of which: yes, I do work for the Merovingian. I run his constructs: coordinating firewalls, maintaining private servers, code maintenance... And our dear leader himself can be very demanding. Makes me wonder why some of the more powerful programs--the Trainman, for instance--put up with him at all. But oh, look at the time. Let's move on to the next room.

done.say: Looks like he's enabled access to the next room.

objective.text: Find the Effectuator in the room after that

talk.say: Oy! How many of this guy are there?

So, my dear dire lupines (Aren't they neat? And so discreet. The Merovingian made them specially for me) indicated that trouble was coming, and I just had to pop in and meet you. Here's the thing: I can't have you meddling with my constructs. I mean, really, do you want to get me fired?
But it wouldn't be right to leave you empty-handed, after you've worked so hard. Let's see... Aha! I'll give you some more lupines to play with; their combat routines have become a little rusty. Check with your operator. See ya!

done.say: Hey! I'm getting a broadcast here. It's the address of a site nearby. I suppose you'll just have to leave your new friend behind for now--since he's insubstantial, there's nothing we can do to him...at the moment.

phase.briefing:
What the friggin' hell kind of fruitcake was that? Apparently this is all some kind of big game to him. We'll just see how much he likes it once we've castrated all his "dear" dire lupines, and trapped his skinny old insubstantial butt in a mez field! And why did he assume that Tyndall is directing you? I'm in charge here! Mr. Fake Tan is in for a nasty surprise.
Take those dogs to the cleaners, and find some way of tracking down the Effectuator.

enter.say:
I wonder if the Effectuator made that Tyndall reference just to get under Anome's skin? Heh.
Looks like he's playing square with us, at any rate; I've got lots of intermittent signals in there, of the dire lupine persuasion, from the looks of it. Does the Effectuator really not care if we waste these guys, or is he hoping to goad us in over our heads?

done.say: That seems to be all of them. Hey, I'm reading something on the body of that last one. See what it is.

objective.text: Get the address from the Dire Lupine Bane's body

done.say: An address? And not far away, either. That's awfully convenient...

phase.briefing: So, you found an address on one of those dogs? Well, what the hell are you waiting for? Do you want the Effectuator to get away? Move it!

enter.say: That's the address. Seems awfully quiet... I'm reading a small local network, but that's about it.

done.say: Hello, operative. Still on the case? I admire your dedication! If you're going to get through my computer system there, I'm afraid you'll find that there's a certain sequence you have to follow. By the way, some mutual friends of ours should be along at any moment. Don't blink!
It sounds like you'll have to search all the computers in there in a specific order. This is-- Heads up!
Still going strong, eh? But you've turned your back again...
More lupines!
I do believe you've done it. I've underestimated you. Well, Architect knows I'm not perfect. C'est la vie!
I'm scanning some data on that machine. Did the Effectuator want us to find it? Well, Anome's chomping at the bit, so I suppose you'd better get it.
What'd you find? Is it something to do with that pathetic clown, the Effectuator? Upload it to me immediately!

objective.text: Upload the information at a hardline

done.say: Uh-oh. From where I'm sitting, that doesn't look like it was regular data...

mission.finish:
What th--? Network activity is going haywire! That "data" you uploaded was a virus! Oh, crap! ...
It's wiping our data on the Effectuator's lupines and construct portals! Uh... We'll get back to you.
Someone get Tyndall! Shut the systems down! Shut everythi--
